name: BlameAttributionTab

states.name: Page Identity and Navigation
states.description: The Blame Attribution tab lives within the Run Recap page's tabbed interface, alongside Timeline, Verification, Knowledge, Context, Canvas, and Errors tabs. Users reach it by clicking the tab after a workflow run completes (or during a run, for live blame data). The tab should clearly communicate its purpose: explaining WHY failures happened, complementing the Verification tab which shows WHAT failed.
states.precondition: User has navigated to the Run Recap page for a completed or in-progress workflow run

states.name: Blame Summary Statistics
states.description: At the top of the Blame tab, aggregate statistics give users an at-a-glance understanding of how many failures were attributed, how many files are oscillating, and how many revert patterns were detected. These numbers come from the GET /task-runs/{id}/blame response fields: total_attributions, total_oscillating_files, total_revert_patterns. Users use these to gauge the severity of convergence problems before diving into per-iteration details.
states.precondition: At least one iteration had verification failures with blame data (blame_json is non-null in at least one IterationResult)

states.name: Per-Iteration Blame Detail
states.description: The core of the Blame tab: a chronological list of iterations that produced blame data. Each iteration section shows which verification steps failed and which previous iteration's changes caused each failure. The data comes from the blame_reports array in the GET /task-runs/{id}/blame response. Each report contains attributions (step name, blamed iteration, implicated files with line ranges, confidence score, explanation). Users read this to understand the causal chain: 'Iteration 3's TypeScript check failed because iteration 2 modified Card.tsx.'
states.precondition: At least one iteration produced blame attributions

states.name: File Oscillation Warnings
states.description: When the blame engine detects that a file has been modified in 3 or more consecutive iterations, it surfaces an oscillation warning. This is a strong signal that the AI is stuck: it keeps changing the same file but the fix never sticks. The UI should make these warnings visually prominent (they represent the most actionable finding in the blame data). The oscillating_files array in each BlameReport contains the file path, the number of consecutive iterations (consecutive_blames), and the specific iteration numbers involved.

states.name: Revert Pattern Warnings
states.description: Revert patterns are detected when a file is modified in a non-consecutive alternating pattern (present, absent, present) across iterations with at least 2 gaps. This indicates the AI's changes are being undone — possibly by other fixes that conflict, or by the AI itself reverting its previous approach. These are shown separately from oscillation warnings because the behavior pattern (intermittent vs consecutive) and the recommended response differ. Revert patterns are excluded for files already flagged as oscillating to avoid duplicate warnings.

states.name: Empty and Loading States
states.description: The Blame tab must gracefully handle cases where no blame data exists — either because the run completed on the first iteration (no failures to attribute), the run is still in its initial verification phase, or blame analysis produced no attributions (all failures had generic error messages with no extractable file paths).
states.precondition: The run completed successfully on the first verification iteration with no failures

states.name: Live Blame Updates During Active Runs
states.description: During an active run, blame data is emitted in real-time via the AppEvent::BlameAttribution Tauri event (event name: 'blame-attribution'). The event payload includes task_run_id, iteration, attributed_failures count, oscillating_files count, revert_patterns count, and the full blame_json. The tab should update incrementally as new iterations complete, without requiring a manual page refresh. This allows users to observe blame accumulation in real-time and intervene early if they see oscillation forming.
states.precondition: The user is viewing the Blame tab for an actively running workflow that has emitted at least one blame-attribution event

states.name: Escalation Policy Status
states.description: The escalation policy (EscalationPolicy struct on LoopConfig) controls warnings and 'rethink' prompts when the loop fails to make progress. warn_after (default: 3) triggers a warning log. rethink_after (default: 5) injects a meta-prompt telling the AI to step back and reconsider its approach — it fires at the threshold, then every 3 iterations after. time_limit_secs enforces a wall-clock deadline checked in CheckPreconditions. The Blame tab should surface escalation events so users understand when and why the system intervened.

states.name: Cross-Tab Referencing
states.description: The Blame tab's value is amplified when users can cross-reference blame data with other Run Recap tabs. Iteration numbers in blame attributions should correlate with the Timeline tab. Failed step names should match entries in the Verification tab. File paths in implicated changes can be correlated with the git diff context shown in the Context tab. This cross-referencing is architectural — it does not require explicit navigation links, but the naming and numbering must be consistent across tabs.
states.precondition: At least one blame attribution exists and the Timeline/Verification tabs are also populated

states.name: Cross-Run Learning Integration
states.description: Blame attributions are recorded as causal events in SQLite via record_blame_as_causal_events() — each attribution becomes a causal edge with cause_type 'iteration_change' and effect_type 'verification_failure', relationship 'caused_by_change'. Oscillation patterns are stored as cause_type 'file_oscillation' / effect_type 'convergence_stuck'. The cross_run_learning.rs module queries these events to detect systemic patterns across runs (e.g., the same file is blamed across multiple independent runs). This is a backend-only integration but the Blame tab should document it for architectural awareness.
states.precondition: The cross_run_learning system has detected that the same file was blamed in 2+ previous runs

description: Blame Attribution Tab — a deep-dive view within the Run Recap page that shows which iteration's code changes caused each verification failure. When the agentic verification loop fails to converge, users need to understand causality: not just which checks failed, but which specific iteration introduced the regression. The blame engine (a deterministic, file-path-based algorithm — no LLM calls) cross-references error output (stdout/stderr from verification steps) against per-iteration git diffs to attribute failures to specific iterations. This tab surfaces blame attributions, oscillation warnings (same file modified 3+ consecutive iterations), revert patterns (change-undo-change cycles), and escalation status. Data comes from the MCP endpoint GET /task-runs/{id}/blame which parses iteration_results.blame_json from the task run's result_data. Real-time updates arrive via the AppEvent::BlameAttribution Tauri event during active runs.
